coverage_override.reason: Optional non-Tuner treatment, banished self-summon, and the Main-Phase summon/Link-lock effect are the three mechanics; the two HOPT clauses attach to the latter two.

effects.printed_clause: If this card you control is used as Synchro Material, you can treat it as a non-Tuner.
effects.lua_implementation: A single-range EFFECT_NONTUNER on the Monster Zone permits this controlled card to be treated as a non-Tuner for its controller's Synchro Summon.

official_references.matched_structure: Official optional non-Tuner treatment for Synchro Material uses EFFECT_NONTUNER and a controller-aware value function.

effects.printed_clause: If you control "Bauy World": You can Special Summon this card from your banishment.
effects.lua_implementation: A banished-zone Ignition Effect checks for face-up Bauy World, an open Monster Zone, and this card's summon legality, then Special Summons it under its HOPT code.

official_references.matched_structure: Official conditioned self-Special Summons from a non-hand location check field state, zone availability, and summon legality.

effects.printed_clause: During the Main Phase (Quick Effect): You can banish this face-up card and 1 card from your hand; Special Summon 1 "Bau" monster from your hand or Deck, except "Bauy Magician", also you cannot Special Summon Link Monsters for the rest of this turn.
effects.lua_implementation: The Main-Phase Quick Effect banishes this face-up card and one hand card as cost, summons another Bau from hand/Deck, then registers an End-Phase-resetting player restriction that now rejects Link Monsters from every location.

official_references.matched_structure: Official post-resolution summon locks use a player-targeted EFFECT_CANNOT_SPECIAL_SUMMON field effect with an End Phase reset.

effects.issue: Confirmed and corrected: the text has no 'from the Extra Deck' qualifier. The old restriction allowed Link Monsters to be revived from the GY or banishment; it now blocks Link Special Summons from any location.
